answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so a node’s influence depends on paths supported by credible links rather than self-issued identities. A sybil cluster—whether labeled opal, glacier, or forge—must connect to the honest graph through an external cut; if that cut is sparse, its conductance is low and few walks escape the cluster. Min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore limit the cluster’s aggregate voting weight.
